data.why: the real dataset is a ~930MB Zenodo download that the sandbox cannot fetch at install, so a script (placed at /work/app/generate_data.py, run during install) writes small netCDF/CSV files on a coarse 7x12 lat/lon grid with the same variable names, dimensions and units the bokeh apps expect, including a missing-retrieval NaN, a bad-pixel spike, a late-installed station with a missing early record, and a sensor-spike outlier.

goals: map the global distribution and multi-decadal trend of surface solar radiation (SSR) and animate it month by month
inspect the deseasonalized SSR anomaly time series and jump to the corresponding global map for any date
compare modelled SSR against GEBA ground-station observations and read evaluation metrics (bias, RMSE, correlation) per station
attribute SSR changes at a location or region to contributing atmospheric drivers (aerosols, clouds, water vapor, ozone) via bar-plot decomposition
examine trends, Pearson/Spearman correlations and significance between SSR and climatic driver variables (temperature, precipitation, sea ice, etc.)

review.summary: The tree captures what EarthSense is for (map SSR and its anomalies, check it against GEBA stations, attribute dimming/brightening to drivers and climate variables), and every sampled screen backs its node. It needs small fixes before filing: add the missing click-a-month-bar-for-that-month's-mean-map interaction the README describes, fold two UI-chore tasks into features, move the non-working multi-station task to not_done, and remove agent-mechanics actions.
